title: Ulster American by David Ireland at Irish Rep #ulsteramerican #matthe...
transcript: A creative process between a writer, a director, and a famous actor can easily get contentious with everyone's egos at play. Throw in a dose of politics and misogyny and it's bound to go poorly. This is the premise of David Ireland's satire Ulster American at Irish Rep. Matthew Broderick stars as an Oscar-winning actor whose intentions are sunny but whose social blindspots are egregious. With just three characters who are all weirdos in their own right, I found this play equally funny and uncomfortable. It sequences its points of conflict very craftily, raising the stakes and digging the characters deeper into disagreement. Matthew Broderick's demeanor in this piece is reserved in a sulky, petulant sort of way, and it becomes increasingly clear over the course of the play just how childishly entitled the character truly is. In reference to this, another character says something like “he's not an adult, he's an actor” which I thought was a fantastic line. It does veer off course at the end, self-detonating unexpectedly and unrealistically after boxing itself into a somewhat unresolvable situation. While this definitely made the play entertaining through its final moment, I felt that it undermined the intelligence that permeated the piece up to that point. Nevertheless, this was a tight 80 minutes that I ultimately found enjoyable. With that, another program for my collection.
